children: Pure One Corporation
has received 24 further orders for its Zeus electric vans, lifting its Australian order book to 33 vehicles less than three months after the range launched.
The orders come from a mixture of dealers and end customers, with the additional vehicles scheduled for delivery during 2027 rather than immediate handover.
Priced between $70,000 and $100,000 each, the Zeus range is being marketed to commercial operators while attracting interest from businesses seeking vehicles for specialist conversions.
Pure One has added dealers in Victoria and Western Australia alongside the latest orders as it works towards a national distribution network.
Continuing Launch Momentum
The latest orders follow nine initial vehicle orders announced in October, giving Pure One an early indication of demand beyond the range’s September Australian launch.
Although the company has not disclosed the value or model mix of the latest purchases, the published price range provides a guide to the scale of individual vehicle sales.
For now, the order book represents future deliveries, and the next commercial test will be converting those commitments into vehicles supplied to customers during 2027.

Rather than relying solely on direct sales, Pure One is widening the channels through which fleet operators and other buyers can assess and purchase the vans, with the company identifying dealer recruitment as a central part of that rollout and a target of 10 outlets by the middle of next year.
Diversity of Applications
“What is particularly encouraging is the diversity of applications being considered for the Zeus range,” managing director Scott Brown said.
“Alongside traditional cargo and commercial transport, we are receiving interest in mobile food vending and RV conversions.”
“This represents a significant addressable market opportunity for Pure, leveraging the unique specifications of the Zeus range to generate sales through different market segments.”

Car Sales Express in Victoria and Londy, trading as Purely Commercials in Western Australia, are the newest appointments to the distribution network, extending the company’s presence into markets where commercial customers may prefer to buy through established local businesses.

Expanding that network could give Pure One a broader route to fleet buyers without depending entirely on a single sales channel, and the company is continuing to seek further dealer appointments as it aims for its mid-2027 network target.
New Customer Market
Another source of interest has emerged through AdventureEV, which has joined Pure One as a customer intending to use Zeus vans for recreational vehicle and campervan conversions.
The specialist designs and manufactures electric campervan fit-outs, making the Zeus platform a potential base for uses beyond conventional cargo movement and passenger transport.
Pure One is promoting the range’s payload capacity of up to 1,890 kilograms as a feature for conversion businesses requiring flexibility in their vehicle layouts.
The proposed cargo and passenger configurations are expected to become available in early 2027, broadly aligning the product rollout with the scheduled deliveries from the new orders.
“Our focus is now on maintaining this sales momentum, expanding our national distribution network, and progressing vehicle deliveries in 2027,” Mr Brown added.

title: Pure One Adds 24 Zeus Electric Van Orders Across Expanding Dealer Network
